As Dubai Medical University (DMU) welcomes students and faculty to the 2026/2027 academic year, the University is officially launching an ambitious phase of digital transformation. Starting this Fall 2026 semester, DMU is integrating advanced AI-enabled educational tools to foster a highly interactive, student-centered learning environment.

A cornerstone of this new initiative is the introduction of the AI Student Assistant, an innovative digital companion designed to support students in their pre-class preparation. By helping learners clarify complex concepts and practice with tailored questions, the AI assistant ensures students arrive at lectures fully prepared. This technology is strategically deployed to complement, not replace, the academic expertise, mentorship, and professional judgment of DMU faculty.

This digital shift is set to significantly strengthen the university’s Flipped Classroom and Team-Based Learning (TBL) frameworks. With students mastering core materials beforehand, faculty can now dedicate valuable classroom time to higher-order application, clinical reasoning, dynamic case-based discussions, and deeper student-faculty engagement. Additionally, faculty are now equipped with AI-supported tools to refine question banks, generate authentic clinical scenarios, provide structured feedback, and analyze learning data to support student success.

To ensure a seamless transition and equip educators with the necessary skills, DMU successfully hosted a comprehensive university-wide faculty workshop on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. The full-day orientation provided practical, hands-on guidance on integrating these tools into daily instruction and assessment.

Dubai Medical University Launches Comprehensive QAIE Portal to Drive Quality and Excellence

Dubai Medical University (DMU) has announced the official launch of its Quality Assurance (QA) Portal, marking a major step forward in digitizing and streamlining QA operations across the institution. This was through a workshop led by Prof. Ibrahim Elsayed, Vice Chancellor – QAIE, and Dr. Eslam ElNebrisi, Director of QAIE. The new portal is designed

Dubai Medical University (DMU) has announced the official launch of its Quality Assurance (QA) Portal, marking a major step forward in digitizing and streamlining QA operations across the institution. This was through a workshop led by Prof. Ibrahim Elsayed, Vice Chancellor – QAIE, and Dr. Eslam ElNebrisi, Director of QAIE.

The new portal is designed to unify all QA processes into one centralized, user-friendly platform that ensures accuracy, transparency, and accessibility. Among its key features are a fully digitized policy repository, a searchable archive of old versions, and a system that allows stakeholders to suggest policy changes — which are then reviewed by relevant authorities before approval by the Deans’ Council.

In addition to policy management, the portal will support DMU’s institutional accreditation efforts, internal reviews, and reporting, while also playing a key role in research and ranking initiatives.
The QAIE team is also rolling out regular workshops to ensure all faculty and staff are trained on using the portal effectively.

The Career Guidance office at Dubai Medical University, College of Medicine, successfully hosted its first TEAM (Trauma Evaluation and Management) Course in collaboration with TraumaUAE, marking an important milestone in advancing trauma education and clinical skills training for future healthcare professionals.

The course brought together medical students, faculty members, and healthcare professionals for a comprehensive learning experience focused on the principles of trauma assessment and early management. Participants engaged in a combination of interactive lectures, hands-on skills training, and simulation-based case scenarios designed to strengthen clinical decision-making, teamwork, communication, and patient-centered care in emergency situations.

The program was delivered by a distinguished team of instructors who provided valuable expertise and practical insights into trauma care. The simulation-based activities, facilitated by the DMU Simulation Center, offered participants the opportunity to apply their knowledge in realistic clinical environments and enhance their confidence in managing trauma cases.

Dubai Medical University extends its sincere appreciation to TraumaUAE, the course faculty, and the DMU Simulation Center for their contributions to the success of this initiative. Special recognition is also extended to the Career Guidance & Alumni Engagement Office for coordinating and organizing the event as part of the university’s commitment to supporting student development and lifelong learning.

September 13 – 2026, Dr. Bassam Atallah, Associate Dean – Clinical Affairs at the College of Pharmacy, Dubai Medical University, participated in the First Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi Cardiovascular Updates Conference, held at Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi on September 12–13, 2026.

Dr. Atallah contributed to the conference through serving as one of the chairs of the “Updates in Special Populations” session. The session featured presentations addressing contemporary management approaches for complex cardiovascular conditions, including transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, and perioperative assessment of complex cardiac patients.

The conference brought together leading cardiovascular specialists to discuss the latest developments in cardiovascular disease management, with a focus on emerging evidence, practice-changing updates, and contemporary therapeutic approaches.

Dubai Medical University (DMU), in collaboration with Project You, a social enterprise dedicated to upskilling future generations, successfully hosted “Project Nightingale”, an immersive three-day workshop designed for students from Al Salam Community School.

Held from October 7–9, the program aimed to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance triage systems in emergency departments, empowering students to apply technology and empathy in healthcare innovation.

The workshop was led by DMU alumni Dr. Tasnima Tayb and Dr. Aisha Ismail, alongside Emergency Medicine Hive Co-chairpersons Dr. Shiza Ali and Asiya Mubeen. Over 60 students from Grades 8 and 9 participated in engaging sessions including:
A mock emergency simulation
An “Empathy Expedition” at the Dubai Medical University Hospital
Campus tours introducing the world of medical education
Design thinking workshops, culminating in a final showcase of AI-powered solutions developed with guidance from DMU mentors.
DMU expressed its appreciation to the Simulation Center—led by Prof. Basil and Dr. Marwa—and to Student Affairs for their unwavering support in bringing this initiative to life.

“Project Nightingale reflected the true spirit of mentorship, innovation, and community that defines Dubai Medical University,” the organizers shared. “We were inspired by the creativity and curiosity of Al Salam Community School’s students and grateful to Project You for this meaningful partnership.”
Special thanks were extended to the dedicated volunteer teams whose enthusiasm and commitment made the event a memorable success.
